The eight-episode follow-up (down from nine) is now in post-production (reshoots are still possible), and while fans are already dreaming of a season 3, Disney+ won’t make any calls until it sees how these new episodes land.
Charlie Cox, Vincent D’Onofrio, Deborah Ann Woll and Wilson Bethel (Bullseye) lead the cast alongside returning favorites like Jessica Jones and newcomer White Tiger. Word is Kingpin’s now the Big Apple’s mayor, and there’s hope for a surprise Elektra cameo. Keep an eye out for the first look dropping at next month’s D23 event.
articles.title: ‘Daredevil: Born Again' Season 2 Wraps Filming

articles.author: TV News
articles.description:
Noah Wyle is officially back on the Emmy radar after a 26-year hiatus: he snagged his first ever Outstanding Lead Actor in a Drama Series nod for Max’s medical drama The Pitt. You might remember him as Dr. John Carter on ER — Wyle was practically an Emmy regular in the late ’90s (five straight supporting-actor noms from 1995–1999) but hasn’t been a contender since his last Carter shout-out in ’99.
The Pitt didn’t stop at Wyle’s big moment, hauling in 13 nominations in its freshman run, from Katherine LaNasa for supporting actress and Shawn Hatosy for guest actor to makeup and directing nods. His toughest competition? Adam Scott in Apple TV+’s Severance. The 77th Primetime Emmys air September 14 on CBS and Paramount+, with Nate Bargatze hosting.
articles.title: Noah Wyle Scores First Emmy Nomination in 26 Years

articles.author: TV News
articles.description:
Disney+’s pint-sized phenom Bluey crushed the competition in H1 2025, racking up a whopping 25 billion minutes watched across 154 episodes to claim the top spot in U.S. household TV streaming. Animation was no flash in the pan, either—half a dozen cartoons made the top 20 list, from Family Guy and SpongeBob SquarePants to Bob’s Burgers and South Park. Grey’s Anatomy and NCIS followed closely behind with 22 billion and 19 billion minutes, respectively.
On the originals front, Netflix’s Squid Game snagged #1 with 15 billion minutes over just 22 episodes, edging out Prime Video’s Reacher and The Night Agent. HBO Max’s The White Lotus and Apple TV+’s Severance also punched above their subscriber weight, while Paramount+ originals 1923 and Landman rounded out the top six. Classics and family flicks held their own, too—Gunsmoke streamed 10.6 billion minutes, and movies like Moana 2, Despicable Me 4, The Wild Robot and Sonic The Hedgehog 2 landed in the top 10.
articles.title: Nielsen: Disney's ‘Bluey' Topped All Household TV Streaming in First Half of 2025 With 25 Billion Minutes
